title: 8-0 becomes 8-1: 'Impatient' PV Sindhu falls to cramping Wang Zhi Yi in epic duel
content: PV Sindhu's World Championships campaign ended in controversy as Wang Zhi Yi overcame cramps, a hostile Delhi crowd and the five-time medallist to snap her unbeaten record against Chinese shuttlers at the Worlds. Ayush Shetty also bowed out, while Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Satwik-Chirag marched into the quarter-finals.

title: Gates Foundation makes landmark 10-yr donation to Washington University to strengthen ...
content: The Gates Foundation has awarded a significant donation to the University of Washington's health institute. This substantial grant will expand the Global Burden of Disease study's reach. IHME will now cover nearly 5,000 locations, providing more detailed local health information. The funding also supports health forecasting and global health spending research efforts. This investment aims to inform critical decisions for improving global health outcomes.

title: How an ex-Buddhist monk & Meta engineer founded a startup that now rivals Accenture
content: Lilly Chen, a former Buddhist monk and Meta software engineer, founded Contenda after a hackathon.  She and three friends turned a pandemic-era project into a successful startup.  The company focuses on helping businesses repurpose technical content effectively.  Contenda secured one million dollars in pre-seed funding in March 2021.  Chen now leads the company as its chief executive officer.

title: Brazilian mother and daughter built seven-bedroom home from 8,000 glass bottles
content: A visionary mother and daughter duo transformed sustainability into an art form, building a seven-room home out of more than 8,000 recycled glass bottles. Incorporating elements like reclaimed wood and toothpaste tubes, this remarkable endeavor addresses the dual challenges of beach pollution and housing shortages in Brazil. Named the Salt House, it stands as a sustainable residence and an inspiring venue for community education on environmental responsibility and innovative reuse.

title: Told he had months to live, Seattle shipbuilder survived another 38 years
content: Robert Moran, Seattle's former mayor, made a monumental gift of thousands of acres for a state park. Following a serious illness, he relocated to Orcas Island, where he developed picturesque forest lands into a personal estate. His visionary donation led to the establishment of Washington's first state park, named Moran State Park in his honor, which remains a beloved destination to this day.

title: Canadian wildfires cut solar power by 6.38 TWh, caused $1.9bn loss in 2023
content: Wildfire smoke significantly reduced solar power generation across North America and Europe. This reduction caused substantial economic losses and increased carbon emissions. Other air pollution sources like automobiles also impact solar panel productivity. Wildfires can also physically damage solar farm equipment and infrastructure. Improved forecasting and vegetation management can mitigate these solar generation challenges.

title: Who is Kyle Clemons, Christina Clemons' husband? His Olympic career and life now
content: Christina Clemons’ husband, Kyle Clemons, is an Olympic gold medalist who competed in the 400 meters and helped the U.S. win the 4x400m relay at Rio 2016. He later entered the food business with Christina through Gold Medal BBQ Co. Christina remains active in track and field and continued racing successfully during the 2026 indoor season.

title: Kevin Owens makes major announcement ahead of Undisputed WWE Championship match
content: Kevin Owens is set to have his parents cheering him on during his championship match in Toronto, a poignant occasion following a tough neck injury recovery. This is especially touching given his mother's health challenges. Owens has fond memories of winning a title while his family watched remotely, and now, nearly two decades later, they will witness his first singles match together live.

title: Who was Ben Conken? College football player dies at 20 after cancer battle
content: Ben Conken, a University of West Florida football player, died Aug. 17 at age 20 after battling cancer. A 2024 Cottage Hill Christian Academy graduate, he played football, baseball and basketball before joining UWF. He was remembered for his athletic ability, strong character and kindness. His school and former team continue to mourn his loss.

title: ABVP, Left-leaning student groups clash on Jadavpur University campus; several injured

Several students sustained injuries during the confrontation, with some requiring hospital treatment. The confrontation reportedly began over a student union meeting and continued late into the night. Both groups accused each other of bringing outsiders onto the university campus. Protests have been announced by both student organizations following the incident.

title: Why UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi' matters more than ever in 2027 assembly election

Parties are actively wooing women with welfare schemes and cash transfers.  Both the BJP and Samajwadi Party are making substantial promises to female voters.  Winning the trust of over six crore women voters will be crucial for electoral success.

title: H-1B visa reality for Indians: Unpredictable costs, tougher odds & greater risks
content: H-1B visas have long been the main road for Indian professionals who are seeking employment, long-term career opportunities, and eventually even the green card in the US. But over the past two years, several changes in the H-1B visa application and selection criterion have added a huge layer of uncertainty.

title: Man posing as transgender sexually assaults air hostess on pretext of 'curing evil eye'

title: After Rana’s demise, Oly medallist Manu forging new bonds with Serbian coach

Jelena says Bhaker’s openness to new ideas reflects her hunger to improve, with the 24-year-old focused on becoming better and more consistent.

title: Joe Root equals Sachin Tendulkar’s record for most fifties in Test cricket

title: Hockey World Cup: India hold England to goalless draw, seal second-round spot

title: Houses damaged in Jammu village subsidence; families take shelter in tents
content:
Heavy rains trigger landslides in Kheri village, residents say several houses damaged (Image: ANI)

JAMMU: Nearly a dozen families have been forced to take shelter in tents after subsidence damaged several houses and sparked panic in Kheri village on the outskirts of Jammu city. “It has become scary to live in a structure on the verge of collapse,” said a resident. Locals demanded the authorities conduct a detailed geological and technical survey of the area to devise a permanent solution to the recurring problem. An official said, “A small chunk of land is facing subsidence, and geological experts are currently conducting a survey.” The area previously witnessed similar subsidence on Sept 13 last year. Local resident Mohammad Javaid said his newly built, two-storey house developed deep cracks last year. Sporadic cases of land subsidence were also reported across 19 locations in Ramban, Kishtwar, Poonch, Reasi, and Kathua districts following heavy rain and flash floods.

End of Article

title: 6.6-magnitude earthquake strikes central Peru
content:
Earthquake in Peru

An earthquake of magnitude 6.6 struck central Peru on Thursday, news agency Reuters reported citing the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said. The quake occurred at a depth of 10 km (6.21 miles), according to GFZ. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage. The tremor was felt across parts of southern Peru, including the regions of Ica and Arequipa. Peru experiences frequent earthquakes as it lies along the Pacific “Ring of Fire”, a zone known for intense seismic activity. A magnitude 7.9 earthquake that struck the Ica region in 2007 killed nearly 600 people.
